body:
This is used in all renderers, not just Mobile/Compatibility. However, it's most useful in Forward+ where light culling is the most aggressive (as it's cluster-based instead of AABB-based).

I would also clarify the fact that when using standard per-pixel shaded materials, the value generally doesn't need to be changed from its default.


```suggestion
				Sets the extra cull margin for this light, allowing it to not get culled by the Forward+ clustering algorithm or the AABB-based algorithm in Mobile and Compatibility. Set along with [member Light3D.light_extra_cull_margin]. This allows lights on vertex-shaded materials or custom light shaders to not get culled early while their influence is still visible on screen. For best performance, this should be set to the lowest possible value that does not result in the light disappearing while its influence is still visible on screen.
				[b]Note:[/b] When using standard per-pixel shaded materials, there is generally no need to increase this value above [code]0.0[/code].
```

body: Why is the description of the RenderingServer method vastly more detailed than the more user-facing new property?

There does need to be something here, because just growing the cone shape won't catch vertices that are to the side of the cone tip or behind it. Since the units of extra_cull_margin are distance rather than angle, the choice of addition does seem arbitrary and might fail at some geometry scales. Maybe this would be more robust:

`(p_type == LIGHT_TYPE_OMNI || (p_type == LIGHT_TYPE_SPOT && (p_spot_aperture > WIDE_SPOT_ANGLE_THRESHOLD_DEG || p_extra_cull_margin > 0)))`

In lieu of finding a separate solution for spot lights that is as robust I decided to utilize the existing codepath that treats wide spots as spheres. Effectively, adding a margin will make that spot light get treated as a omni light for the culling and so it guarantees none of it gets culled early.

The RenderingServer documentation was added by @Calinou on a suggestion here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112098#discussion_r3035808012

It's not clear to me how much detail should or should not be in the user-facing tooltip.

I think it'd be better if any margin forced it to be treated as an omni light, like @pshaughn's suggestion. Having it culled as a spot light doesn't sound like it'll ever work correctly. So the user would have to heavily increase the margin to get it treated as an omni light anyway, which would cause the culling radius to excessively get expanded.
